_header: ===== cherrypick-pmcc — PMCC-99 deep-ITM covered calls on leveraged ETFs (paper-only) =====
_what_this_is: Buy the deepest ~99-delta call at ~21 DTE (a stock substitute with near-zero extrinsic — NOT a LEAP), sell an ITM call at ~9 DTE whose intrinsic is the downside buffer and whose time value is the entire profit; when the short's time value is exhausted (~$0.10), close BOTH legs and re-enter. Three books, one variable each: `control` (mechanical entry, hold-on-breach, never roll), `keltner` (control's management, entry gated on a pullback-and-reversal read of the Keltner channel), `roll` (control's entry, rolls the short down/out on a breach). Early assignment is REFUSED-around and MEASURED, never modelled — see the dividends block and the assignment_exposure_tv knob. Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or ~/.cherrypick/config/pmcc.json.
_symbols_note: Leveraged index ETFs with $1 strikes and weekly expirations: TNA (Russell 2000 3x), TQQQ (Nasdaq-100 3x), UPRO (S&P 500 3x). One position per (symbol, book) at a time — max_positions bounds each book to the symbol count. All American physical delivery; a symbol not declared in settlement_style is refused at entry (unknown_settlement).
_occ_roots_note: The OCC root the provider admits per underlying. Leveraged ETFs split often, and a split leaves ADJUSTED roots (TNA1) sharing expiration dates with the standard root; only the configured root is priced, and an expiration listing only adjusted roots refuses `not_root_listed`. After a split, verify the standard root re-lists before resuming — and treat a split mid-position as a manual `--settle` plus a measurement break (unmodelled).
_settlement_style_note: How each underlying's expiring legs settle. All three are `physical` — American delivery: an ITM short call hands over 100 short shares per contract at the settlement print, covered the NEXT session together with the long's sale (the combined disposal), so a Friday assignment carries short shares over the weekend. Delivered shares are booked at the SETTLEMENT SPOT, not the strike — the calendars decomposition, which keeps physical settlement exactly cash-plus-a-share-leg. A symbol declared as neither style is refused at entry.
_dividends_note: Entries whose short leg spans a declared ex-dividend date are REFUSED (ex_dividend_span): a short ITM call is really assigned at the close BEFORE the ex-date, and this module deliberately does not model early assignment. Dates are DECLARED from each issuer's own distribution schedule (Direxion for TNA, ProShares for TQQQ/UPRO — all three distribute quarterly, ex-dates in late Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) and never computed or fetched. REFRESH THIS BLOCK QUARTERLY: a span past `declared_through` refuses entry (dividend_calendar_lapsed) rather than assuming itself dividend-free, so a lapsed table stops entries loudly, by design. The example ships declared through August only — August sits between the June and September distributions — so the first refresh is due before mid-September entries; fill in the September ex-dates from the issuer pages when you do.
_source_note: stream_cache_db overrides the shared stream cache path; null means the suite default (~/.cherrypick/data/marketdata/stream_cache.db). This module is a pure READ-ONLY consumer of that cache — its two expirations are served by the streamer's `expirations` request field, and its deep strikes by the `window_hints` field, both declared automatically every tick.
_dte_note: The short lands on the soonest Friday with DTE in [short_dte_min, short_dte_max] (~9 days); the long on the Friday in [long_dte_min, long_dte_max] nearest long_dte_target (~21 days). Computed from the calendar, asserted against the cache — never nearest-matched from the chain.
_selection_note: long_delta_min + max_long_extrinsic define 'deep': the long is the HIGHEST strike below spot with extrinsic ≤ max_long_extrinsic $/share and (where greeks exist) delta ≥ long_delta_min; with no greeks on file the extrinsic bound alone selects and the row records long_selected_by='extrinsic' so degraded entries stay excludable. target_weekly_yield_min is the short-strike search's floor: the DEEPEST ITM strike whose net time value yields at least this per week on the net debit (max protection subject to yield) — a richer market is simply taken, and the achieved yield is recorded on every entry so any ceiling question is answerable read-side. yield_unreachable refusals record the best yield the chain actually offered.
_management_note: tv_close_threshold: when the short's time value decays to this ($/share) with spot still above the strike, BOTH legs close together (the strategy's one exit; never roll — except the roll book). assignment_exposure_tv: marks with short extrinsic under this are flagged assignment-exposed — pure telemetry bounding what unmodelled early assignment could have touched. disposition_time is when delivered shares are covered and orphan longs sold the session after a settlement. exec_window_start gates ALL management action until the open stabilizes; max_leg_spread_pct is the is-this-mark-actionable bar (deep-ITM spreads on leveraged ETFs are the module's known risk #2 — the attempts table measures how often this refuses).
_window_note: deep_window_pct bounds the entry snapshot's quote fetch: strikes in [spot*(1-deep_window_pct), spot*1.02]. The 99-delta long lives 30-45% below spot, so this, via stream_window's window_hints, is what makes the module's quotes exist at all.
_books_note: `control` is the strategy as taught: mechanical entry whenever its (symbol, book) slot is free, hold the short while ITM, close both legs at tv_close_threshold, hold like a covered call on a breach, never roll. `keltner` differs ONLY in entry timing: spot within keltner_mid_band_atr x ATR of the channel midline (20-EMA of daily closes) AND above yesterday's close AND bounced ≥ keltner_bounce_atr x ATR off today's low. It refuses everything for its first ~keltner_min_history trading days while daily bars accumulate — the cold start is design, not failure. `roll` differs ONLY in breach handling: it rolls the short down/out (once per position per session, same yield search at the current spot) instead of holding, and closes (roll_exhausted) once the long is under min_long_dte_for_roll days. control/roll share fills by construction (exact pairing); keltner deliberately does not — its variable IS the entry tick.
_stream_window_note: How wide an ATM window this module asks the producer for (window_hints). base_width mirrors the streamer's own default; the structural need is computed from the cached chain (strikes down to spot*(1-deep_window_pct) plus margin) and flies-style escalation on no_deep_itm_long / missing_leg_quotes refusals rides on top, decaying when quiet. The union across modules takes the max per symbol, so this can never narrow anyone else.
_tastytrade_costs_note: Overrides for the shared cost model (cherrypick.core.fees.DEFAULT_COSTS): slippage_frac_of_spread, slippage_cap_frac_of_mid, commissions. Empty means the suite defaults. The per-symbol pieces are automatic: ETFs carry no broad-based index exchange fee, each ITM expiry costs the $5 settlement/assignment event, and a physical assignment adds the SEC/FINRA pass-throughs on the share side.
advice_header: ===== the advised book (paper only, off by default) =====
_advice_note: When enabled AND the suite's advisor covers this module (advisor.modules.pmcc in the orchestrator config — both switches must agree), the session's admitted advice opens an `advised:<base_book>` book beside the base, with the admitted params FROZEN on each row at entry and restated through management.effective_params at every later tick. Bounds cover the exit threshold and the entry yield floor; the roll-vs-hold choice is NOT advisable — it is the book contrast, not a parameter.
live_header: ===== live gate (placeholder — see the module CLAUDE.md's Live-trading prerequisites) =====
_live_note: This module has NO live loop, no order-placement code, and no live account designation. `enabled` exists only so the suite's config/console surfaces can read a real gate for this module instead of reporting an absent one as 'unknown' — flipping it to true does nothing until a live loop is built, and post-assignment management plus a calculated ex-div decision (the module CLAUDE.md's prerequisites) land first. Guarded the same as every other live gate: hand-edit only, never through the settings surface.
